collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Children find rubbish piling up by the freshwater spring: organize a cleanup, or ask the adults to stop it at the source.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and the other children have found rubbish piling up by the spring: broken pots, fish bones, old rags, even a strange soft clear thing that washed up from the sea. The spring water is starting to taste odd. (friend) says the adults are to blame. What should the children do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The children clear the spring in a day, carrying every scrap to the midden. They make a sign of shells: keep it clean. The adults are embarrassed and impressed. The water tastes better within a week.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) and the children go to the gathering and ask who has been throwing rubbish by the spring. Several adults go red. A rule is made. The adults clean it up themselves, which the children supervise very strictly.
